newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar cancels 30,000T US corn/soy tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar cancels 30,000T US corn/soy tender.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp cancelled a Friday tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean due to the government ban on pork export, company buyers said.

Taiwan's cabinet-level Council of Agriculture on Thursday banned all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the deadly and highly contagious foot and mouth disease in the island's hog population.
Japan's Agriculture Ministry on Friday banned Taiwan's pork imports indefinitely due to the outbreak.
South Korea also announced a similar ban.
Taiwan's pork exports to Japan comprise about 69 percent of the island's total pork exports.

The Taiwan council estimated that Taiwan breeds 14 million hogs per year. According to a 1994 survey, the industry totalled T$89 billion (US$3.24 billion), or about 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
Taiwan grain buyers estimated on Thursday that a disease-linked ban on pork exports would cause the island's imports of feed corn to fall by about one-fifth.
"Corn imports will drop significantly," one buyer said.

A survey of five major Taiwan grain importers found that all expected significant reductions in corn imports, with most estimating the downturn at about 1.2 million tonnes or 19 percent of the island's annual imports of 6.5 million tonnes.

Taiwan has been importing almost all of its corn from the United States, although recent high U.S. prices have prompted some importers to look to alterative sources in South America, particularly Argentina.
